# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE INTRIGUERS (Harold Bindloss, 1914)

**Cast:** Margaret Keith (elderly, tall, silver hair, prominent nose, piercing eyes, blunt, childless widow, collects small American animals). Mrs. Ashborne (her companion/friend). Millicent Graham (short, slender, brown hair and eyes, delicate prettiness, quiet; daughter of Eustace Graham, a dissipated gambler/"plucker of pigeons" who died; raised by two Evangelical aunts; went to London to nurse him). Richard "Dick" Blake (ex-sapper, Lieutenant, cousin of Bertram; Irish father reckless sportsman, broke neck hunting; mother was Colonel's sister; disgraced after night attack on Indian frontier, blamed for retreat, acquitted at inquiry, left service; blue eyes, dark-blue; brown face; sports "Blake gift" of getting by without money). Bertram Challoner (Captain, painter, son of Colonel Challoner; married Blanche Newcombe at Thornton Holme, Shropshire; sensitive, nervous). Blanche Challoner (young bride). Colonel Challoner (Dick's uncle, austere, Sandymere estate). Cyrus P. Harding (American, paint/varnish traveler, Connecticut factory; wife Marianna, two-room tenement, $200 wedding money; chemistry self-taught; seeks northern gum for varnish; sharp, sanguine, tidy). Clarke (sinister ex-doctor, struck off after police-court affair; lives at Sweetwater homestead; Indian remedies; studies occult with Northern Stonies; drug user; extorts Benson). Benson (ex-Indian army lieutenant, drunk, Peshawur, ghazees; owns farm mortgaged to Clarke; ~£2000). Gardner (Sweetwater store/hotel keeper). Thomas Foster and Mrs. Foster (Hazlehurst, Shropshire). Lieutenant Walters/"Jimmy" (Mrs. Foster's cousin). Greythorpe (Colonel's friend). Sergeant Lane and Private Walthew (RNWMP); Emile (half-breed driver); Robertson (Scot Hudson Bay agent); Dr. Onslow; Miss Challoner (Colonel's sister).

**Events in order:**
1. Quebec, July. Mrs. Keith and Mrs. Ashborne in Dufferin Avenue. Keith plans Montreal by special boat. Millicent's bobcat escapes basket. Morning Post notice of Challoner wedding. Keith tells Dick's disgrace story: night attack, advanced post, officer lost nerve, retreat, Dick blamed. Millicent recalls London flat scene: Eustace's drunken guests, electric light out, Dick defends her, Eustace urges her to leave.
2. River boat from Quebec, night. Dick catches Millicent at gangplank. On deck with baskets, Dick recognizes her; "I'm no longer Lieutenant Blake." Millicent tells of aunts. Dick arranges deckhand to watch animals.
3. Montreal, Windsor Hotel. Challoners arrive. Mount Royal lookout: Dick appears from cable railway; Bertram says "Dick!" Dick: went Penang, Queensland pearl station, East Africa, prairie farming, now "on business" with an American partner. Invited to dinner.
4. Dick tells Bertram goodbye, refuses his money. Challoners leave by Pacific Express. Rotunda: Harding shows red-cedar varnish to lumbermen; Hudson Bay agent. Clarke overhears; cures agent's ague; tells of Stonies, Jack-pine River, Wild-goose hills. Harding: "hoodoos and fakirs."
5. Dick in black cloak with bobcat drops in rotunda. Mrs. Keith questions him; Dick admits he rescued bobcat via taxidermist. Keith knows his name. Harding tells Keith the sandbag story (Blake ran to his aid, later rumor said he ran). Millicent and Dick on hill; he asks for a memento; she gives him a small bunch of flowers from her lace; he keeps them in his pocketbook.
6. Prairie, Sweetwater. Storm. Gardner joins them. Benson drunk, mentions Peshawur, ghazees, Colonel, Bolsover. Farmer warns of Clarke and Dubokars. Clarke arrives at Imperial Hotel; Harding: "something queer about that fellow."
7. Farmer advises taking Benson; Clarke ruining him. Blake visits Clarke's homestead: Clarke offers Blake money-making scheme to squeeze Colonel over the frontier disgrace; Blake refuses; Clarke gives directions for $50.
8. Timber belt. Benson drinks, runs. Blake chases him, threatens pack lariat; Benson returns.
9. Prospectors trade horses; talk of oil and gas. Clarke appears at night camp; claims visit to Stonies; tells his own disgrace story. Harding: suspects Clarke.
10. Muskeg valley; Blake gets malaria, delirious, says "Bertram very good fellow." Indian arrives, reports Stony village location. Harding decides to abduct Clarke, leaves Blake with Benson.
11. Harding and Indian guide reach Stony village. Clarke in tepee with lab apparatus. Harding threatens; Clarke's cough signals friends; Harding trips on bottle, pistol fails to fire.
12. Clarke treats Blake: draught vs. cold water; Blake recovers. Clarke gives "that's all the fee I need offer" line; Clarke leaves with Indian guide, malignant look.
13. Shropshire, November. Thomas Foster in study; Margaret Keith and Millicent visit Hazlehurst; Lieutenant Walters admires Millicent. Sandymere: Colonel and Greythorpe discuss Dick; Colonel shows father's photo (Irish rider). Shrubbery; picture gallery; Millicent praises tarn painting by "my son" (Bertram). Colonel: duty must be done.
14. Clarke visits Colonel with card "Sweetwater." Clarke reveals frontier story: Bertram was on ridge; bugler order; Dick and Bertram two hours alone under arrest. Clarke demands £5000, then £10,000 in oil syndicate shares; Colonel refuses; Clarke's "Blake won't come back." Colonel cables Montreal friend to trace Blake.
15. Clarke at homestead, winter; plots against Blake and Benson; lists Bertram returning from India. Harding, Blake, Benson on north march; gum fails; gasoline smell; Blake goes caribou hunting; wolves; Benson keeps watch.
16. Blake shoots caribou at night, cuts meat, caches in tree; blizzard; reaches camp. Harding's leg injured.
17. Hudson Bay post; Harding burns the gum. Robertson, Scot agent: "no gum of this kind in the timber belt"; oil 300 miles south.
18. Three weeks at post. Dog-team journey south with half-breed guide, then on foot. Route changed SW to Stony village. Blower of natural gas at night; Harding's optimism about oil.
19. Stony village deserted; blizzard three days; Lane, Walthew, Emile (RNWMP patrol). Aurora. Trek back.
20. Clarke's frozen body found under snow; Lane investigates. Harding has taken Clarke's flask (crude petroleum, gasoline distillates) and Colonel's letter to Clarke ("I have nothing further to say..."). Harding plans petroleum claim. Blake reads letter; Harding infers Clarke set trap.
21. Bob-sled with Tom and boys sent by Colonel via Gardner; Colonel's letter begs Blake to come home (Clarke's claim). Harding and Benson partners in oil plan; Harding to raise money.
22. Hazlehurst: Blake meets Millicent; tells of Canada; Mrs. Keith: "Dick, you're the Challoners' pride"; she asks what he'll do.
23. Sandymere: Blake uses chessmen to show frontier attack (Bertram's position on ridge, bugler too far). Colonel convinced; "I'm glad you are my nephew." Blake refuses inheritance.
24. Blake's visit; Colonel's illness (pneumonia); Blake stays; Mrs. Keith advises Millicent to propose; Blake loves Millicent but feels dishonorable. Blake sails in days later; cablegram from Harding: "Come. Struck it. Tell Challoner." Colonel had sent Harding £500 and option on shares.
25. Engagement at Sandymere (Benares brassware pretext). Colonel's reaction; Mrs. Keith approves. Blake sails; work on oil; Harding goes to cities; cablegram: "Bertram killed in action. Challoner." Blake back in England; Millicent meets him; Mrs. Keith has taken house near Sandymere; Colonel frail. Blake keeps secret until Colonel dies; Millicent: "You are brave enough to take this generous part!" END.

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE DATCHET DIAMONDS (Richard Marsh, c. 1900s)

**Cast:** Daisy Strong (Miss Strong, Brighton, companion/friend of Charlie; ~£120 a year from mother; sweetheart of Cyril). Charlie (Charlotte) Wentworth (30, writer for Fashion and other columns, pince-nez, blunt, ~£500 a year; housemate of Daisy at Medina Villas). Cyril Paxton (broker/speculator, handsome, sensitive; heavily invested in Eries, bought 10,000 Trumpit Gold Mine shares; hotel: Makell's, Brighton). Mr. Lawrence / Reginald Hargraves, "The Toff" (fair, pink-white, blue eyes, soft voice, gentle manners; meets Daisy on Devil's Dyke via umbrella; proposes to Daisy; leader of gang). The Baron / Isaac Bergstein (tall thin German-American, stoop, long black overcoat, huge hat, aquiline nose, rolled mouth, clawlike finger, revolver; enraged; shot at Paxton). Skittles (small ex-bruiser, pail; tortured Paxton; branded). John Ireland (Scotland Yard detective, famous; warrant for Paxton). Franklyn (Daisy's and Cyril's lawyer/friend, 40, grey-streaked black hair, grey-black eyes). Hollier (police officer shadowing Franklyn). Treadwater (Makell's manager). Bill Cooper (informer, shabby, billycock; names "Tom the Toff" and "the Baron"). Eversleigh (Datchet servant with short-sighted spectacles; victim of switch). The Duchess of Datchet (Windsor visit; diamonds stolen). Duke of Datchet. Major characters' items: Amsterdam Necklace (~£100,000), Datchet Tiara, Begum's Brooch, Banee's Bracelet, ring (diamond hoop). Total ~£250,000.

**Events in order:**
1. Brighton pier, evening. Daisy meets Lawrence (first on Devil's Dyke, Masonic Ball at Dome, five dances). Cyril confronts; "Who is Mr. Lawrence?" Cyril: "I've gone a bull on Eries... I'm going for the gloves" (big gamble; emigrating next week if loses). Daisy: "I hope you'll win." Kiss.
2. Train to London/ Brighton: Paxton reads Datchet diamond robbery (Windsor, despatch box, Bartlett's Bank, Grosvenor Square; box found empty). Paxton overhears through partition: Lawrence and German-American; Lawrence swapped Gladstone bags using duplicate spectacle case photographed by friend; Eversleigh (short-sighted, spectacles from duke) lost box. Paxton realises Eversleigh's box was the one stolen.
3. Brighton: Paxton and Lawrence in refreshment room; Lawrence offers drink, Paxton refuses. In hotel, Paxton opens wrong Gladstone: rings, tiara, Amsterdam Necklace hidden in shirts. Hides them in newspaper in the bag; goes to find Daisy.
4. Pier: Paxton says he may get a quarter-million; Daisy proposes marriage ("Whither thou goest"); marriage within month. Charlie insults Paxton (ruin; "crossing-sweep"). Paxton storms out; Daisy scolds him.
5. Bodega bar: Lawrence and Baron confront Paxton: "What was the colour of your Gladstone bag, eh?" Ireland appears; warns that diamonds unsaleable, "lifer." Ireland hints he knows Paxton.
6. Night walk: Paxton shadowed by two men. Makell's Hotel: smoking-room stranger questions him. Night: lock picked, then window ladder; Paxton fires revolver through window; ladder left; lantern shattered.
7. Morning: Paxton to London; shadow with cigar; constable called; pushed on platform, pockets searched. Diamonds deposited in Chancery Lane Deposit Company safe.
8. Paxton, back in Brighton, reads Trumpit shares at £10. Dinner interrupted; kidnapped by chloroform outside hotel. Hotel told a fake messenger came for his bag ("Medina Villas").
9. Daisy waits on pier; Lawrence tells her Paxton is in town at Criterion bar; proposes to her; she says she is engaged to Paxton. Charlie & Daisy quarrel.
10. Franklyn arrives: Trumpit shares £12 10s; Cyril's 10,000 shares in his strongbox. Franklyn goes to Makell's; Ireland holds warrant: Paxton wanted for diamond robbery; bet £100 even that Paxton has guilty knowledge. Hollier assigned to follow Franklyn.
11. Daisy confronts Franklyn and Charlie, accuses them of doubting Cyril; breaks with Charlie. Daisy and Charlie go to Makell's.
12. Makell's: Ireland searches Paxton's Gladstone; finds nothing; manager says Paxton took valuables to London. Daisy scolds Ireland. Ireland leaves man. Bill Cooper approaches Ireland: "Tom the Toff" and "the Baron" nicked diamonds; Paxton kidnapped; they'll murder him. Ireland and Daisy go with Cooper to police; drive to crib.
13. Cellar/ hideout: Paxton tied; Skittles splashes water; Baron enters; questions on bag and diamonds. Baron shoots near Paxton's ear; wounds cheek.
14. Lawrence enters; Baron's shooting stopped; Lawrence confesses theft, asks for diamonds; Paxton refuses. Lawrence threatens; orders branding-iron "thief."
15. Branding iron heated. Paxton burns through cords with red-hot iron, takes it; clubs Skittles, shoots Baron (revolver misfires for Lawrence), clubs Lawrence unconscious with revolver butt; sets lamp on fire; flees up steps into pantry cul-de-sac; shouts for help; hears "Hollo!" response.
16. Villains flee in cart; fire spreads; Paxton writes will in blood/pencil: "I give and bequeath all that I have in the world to my dear love, Daisy Strong... CYRIL PAXTON."
17. Ireland's party stops fleeing cart on road; captures prisoners. Daisy finds Paxton's hand at window, grabs will; rescues him.
18. Paxton recovers at Charlie's house, under police guard. Confesses all; diamonds found in safe; Duchess pleased. Trial: Hargraves (Lawrence/Toff) and Bergstein (Baron) 20 years' penal servitude; others shorter. Cooper and Paxton witnesses.
19. Paxton sells shares, invests in consols; marries Daisy quietly at Brighton church. Daisy's "feminine logic": he is unworthy; she threatens to drown; reconciled. Paxton: "God grant that I may never again be led into such temptation!" END.
